I did only brief reading into the power requirements for a Pi, and had a 5V 2A Samsung charger plug around and figured I would be good-to-go. Was surprised as to why I kept seeing the rainbow square every now and then even without being overclocked.

I have about 7 different microUSB-to-USB cords lying around. They're all microUSB, and all fit the Pi and plug into the charger base. They vary slightly in lengths.

But out of these 7 cables, only 2 of them allow me to use the Pi without ever seeing the rainbow square. The others either briefly show the square during boot, or continuously show the square after boot, and 1 or 2 even prevented my USB keyboard from working. This was all from the same Samsung charger plug, and could be reproduced from a Nexus 7 2013 charger plug too.

One of the cords was from a Nexus 7 2013 (original ASUS OEM cord; wasn't the shortest cord I tested). The other was one of a few Samsung cords I had (which was close to the longest cord I tested).

Figured I would be all-set in terms of chargers for the Pis I planned on buying, but now I know I need to also buy some new chargers and cables too :p

This is on a Pi 2 B+ also. 8GB SD card + Composite RCA cable + Ethernet. Keyboard is a Saitek Eclipse with LED backlight. Turbo OC used.
PSA: The USB cord (not just the plug part) matters as to how well power delivery to the Pi is

I am guessing this probably has something to do with the gauge of the wire used in the USB cords. Some of the cheaper cords use thinner gauge wire which may not allow to the PI to pull the power it needs.
2A @ 5V would require very little resistance to limit the flow, you may also want to look at your connections.

My Issue

A dangerous view on how moderating should be.

In the announcement post, Atko has stated that he will not "support subverses with moderators who impose questionable rules such as 'your post has to end with a questionmark'". The problem with this view is that it is highly subjective, since it cannot really be properly defined, objectively, what is and isn't 'questionable'.

For example, in my sub, /v/seriousdiscussion, I have set the tone of the sub early on to reflect a strictly serious environment void of low effort, irrelevant comments and posts to protect a value I held early on in Voat. In order to protect this tone, I implemented a few 'questionable' rules that I thought were objective enough so they would be unabusable and protect the values that the sub was founded on. Granted, a lot of leeway is given to many posts and comments depending on how popular they are.

I would like to press the community here for their thoughts on this issue.
